Published analysis: Extract FG Min 79, Color (SRM) 2.1-2.6, Moisture % Max 4.2, Protein Total 12.0 ± 1.5, Usage Rate up to 100%. Colour here is the midpoint of the published band. PPG is the published minimum fine-grind extract converted at 46.2 points per pound-gallon (pure sucrose): 79% of 46.2 is 36.5, and 36 is kept as the conservative floor, since 79 is a guaranteed minimum rather than a typical.
fermentables.sourceNote:

An industry-wide number was not substituted for the maltster's silence — the American Malting Barley Association's Malting Barley Breeding Guidelines (Ideal Commercial Malt Criteria, revised April 2025) were checked and are now two-row only, carrying adjunct-brewing, all-malt and grain-distilling columns with no six-row column at all.

fermentables.attribution: Briess retired briess.com/malt/<slug> (all 404) and its replacement brewingwithbriess.com/product/<slug>/ 301s to the catalogue rather than a product page — so the citation now points at the Product Information & Specification Bulletin PDF, which is the actual primary datasheet and carries the typical analysis: extract dry basis, colour in SRM, moisture, protein and diastatic power in Lintner. Each PDF was fetched and confirmed before being written.
fermentables.diastaticPowerNote: Its maltster prints no diastatic power for this malt, and for a malt stewed in the husk or roasted this is the expected omission rather than a gap: the enzymes are denatured by the heat that makes the colour and flavour, which is why crystal and roasted malts are steeped or mashed for extract and never relied on to convert anything. Recorded as zero so that a grist calculation counts its weight against the enzyme supply instead of ignoring it. Any residual activity in the more lightly kilned members of this group is small and unmeasured here, so zero is the conservative figure, not a precise one.

fermentables.name: Dextrin Pilsner (Carapils DE)
fermentables.description: German dextrine malt for foam and mouthfeel in pale lagers.
fermentables.attribution: BESTMALZ's published specification for BEST Caramel® Pils. Extract on dry substance is given as not less than 75.0%, which is 34.5 ppg; the stored 33 was below the maltster's own guaranteed minimum and has been raised to it. Wort colour is given as 3.0-7.0 EBC / 1.6-3.1 Lovibond, so the midpoint is 2.35 against a stored 2. Moisture max 4.5%, protein max 12.0% dry basis, wort pH 5.0-5.8.
fermentables.sourceNote: The record's name needs explaining. Carapils® is a Weyermann registered trademark (and separately a Briess one in the US), so "Carapils DE" is not a BESTMALZ product name. BEST Caramel® Pils is their malt of that type, and their own description matches what the record is for - it gives "more full-bodiedness without intensifying their colour" because the caramel sugars in it cannot be fermented. Its 3.0-7.0 EBC also matches the class. The maltster backs extract and colour and nothing else on this record. The maximum batch percentage is this project's own guidance.

fermentables.name: High DP Distillers Malt
fermentables.description: Rahr's distilling malt, kilned to keep the enzymes: over 220 °Lintner, roughly twice a standard 2-row. The malt you reach for when the mash is mostly corn.
fermentables.usageNotes: The point of it is converting somebody else's starch. At 220 °Lintner a 10% charge carries about 22 °Lintner across the whole grist on its own, which is why bourbon mash bills can run 70-80% corn and still convert.
fermentables.attribution: Rahr Malting Co.'s own info sheet for High DP Distillers Malt, which prints Diastatic Power >220 L, Color (SRM) 2.5-3.0, Moisture % Max 6.5, Protein Total <15.0 and Usage Rate up to 100%. Colour here is the midpoint of the sheet's band. PPG is derived from the extract published on the product page (Extract FG Min 76) at 46.2 points per pound-gallon: 76% of 46.2 is 35.1.
fermentables.sourceNote: Rahr's product page and Rahr's own info sheet for this malt do not agree, and rather than quietly pick one, both are recorded. They agree exactly on the figure that matters here — Diastatic Power >220 L — and on usage rate. They differ on colour (page 2.6-3.3 SRM, sheet 2.5-3.0) and on moisture (page max 4.5%, sheet max 6.5%). The sheet's figures are the ones stored, because the sheet is the analysis document. Extract appears only on the page, and protein only on the sheet, so neither document alone supports this record.

additionalSources.supports: Extract FG Min 76, which the info sheet does not print and from which the ppg on this record is derived.
additionalSources.doesNotSupport: Colour and moisture, where it disagrees with Rahr's own info sheet — it prints 2.6-3.3 SRM and max 4.5% moisture against the sheet's 2.5-3.0 and max 6.5%. The sheet's figures are stored.

fermentables.name: GN Zero High Enzyme Distillers Malt
fermentables.diastaticSpecSource: rahr-2026/Rahr GN Zero™ High Enzyme Distillers Malt
fermentables.description: The highest diastatic power in this catalogue at 200-300 °Lintner, malted to hold glycosidic nitrile below 0.5 g/tonne — Rahr's answer to ethyl carbamate control in bourbon.
fermentables.usageNotes: Two jobs at once: enzyme supply for a heavily adjuncted mash, and a low-GN malt for distillers working to reduce ethyl carbamate in the spirit. Alpha amylase is published separately at >80 DU, which is the figure that matters for liquefying a cereal mash.
fermentables.attribution: Rahr Malting Co.'s own spec sheet for GN Zero High Enzyme Distillers Malt, which prints Diastatic Power (DP) 200 - 300 °L, Alpha Amylase (DU) >80, Extract FG Min 78, Protein Total <15%, Moisture % Max <6.5% and GN (g/tonne) <0.5 ppm. Diastatic power here is the midpoint of the published band. PPG is the published minimum extract at 46.2 points per pound-gallon: 78% of 46.2 is 36.0.
fermentables.sourceNote: Colour is not on the spec sheet. It comes from Rahr's product page for the same malt, which prints Color °Lovibond 1.8 - 2.3; the stored 2.05 is that band's midpoint.

additionalSources.supports: Color °Lovibond 1.8 - 2.3, which the spec sheet does not print.
additionalSources.doesNotSupport: The diastatic power, extract, protein, moisture and glycosidic-nitrile figures, which are taken from the spec sheet itself.

fermentables.name: Diastatic Barley Malt
fermentables.description: Weyermann's enzyme supplier — the one malt in their brewery catalogue for which they publish a diastatic power at all, at min 300 WK. Sold for whisky, grain spirit and grain vodka.
fermentables.usageNotes: Weyermann recommend up to 60%. Their own description is unusually direct about what it is for: "the natural and highly effective enzyme supplier for any application that requires large amounts of amylolytic enzymes".
fermentables.attribution: Weyermann's brewery products catalogue (Crop 2025), page 49 of the PDF. Published analysis: Diastatic power min 300 WK, Extract (dry substance) min 78%, Color 2.5-4 EBC / 1.4-2 Lovibond, Moisture max 7%, Protein 9-12.5%, Kolbach Index 38-45%, Saccharification time max 15 min, Friability min 78%. Colour here is the midpoint of the published Lovibond band. PPG is the published minimum extract at 46.2 points per pound-gallon: 78% of 46.2 is 36.0. The diastatic power is converted from Weyermann's WK figure by (WK + 16) / 3.5 = 90.3 °Lintner — the relation verified in data/fermentables/maltster-specs.json against Simpsons, who publish both scales for the same malt.
fermentables.sourceNote: This is the only malt in Weyermann's 63-page brewery catalogue that carries a "Diastatic power" row. Every other Weyermann malt in this catalogue records the qualitative "Enzyme activity" line instead, because that is all Weyermann publishes for them.

fermentables.name: High-Enzyme Malt
fermentables.description: Great Western's distilling malt, and the highest alpha amylase published anywhere in this catalogue at 110 DU alongside 260 °Lintner.
fermentables.usageNotes: Alpha amylase is what liquefies a cereal mash, and on a bourbon bill running mostly gelatinised corn it is usually the binding constraint rather than total diastatic power. Great Western publish both, which few maltsters do.
fermentables.attribution: Great Western Malting's own sell sheet for High-Enzyme Malt, which prints DIASTATIC POWER 260, ALPHA AMYLASE (DU) 110 and MOISTURE (%) 5.5. Colour and protein come from the product page, which prints Color SRM 1.5-2.2 and Protein 14; the stored colour is that band's midpoint.
fermentables.sourceNote: This record carries NO ppg, and that is deliberate rather than an oversight. Great Western publishes no extract figure for this malt — not on the sell sheet, not on the product page — so there is nothing to derive one from, and a plausible number would be an invention. A recipe using this malt will therefore under-count its gravity contribution; the builder warns when an ingredient on the mash path has no extract figure, so that the gap is visible rather than silent.

additionalSources.supports: Color SRM 1.5-2.2 and Protein 14, which the sell sheet does not print.
additionalSources.doesNotSupport: Extract. Neither this page nor the sell sheet publishes one, which is why this record has no ppg.
